title: Cohorted safety-gradient experiment: automated batching & KV-prefetch rollouts with live rollback gates
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: validate an automated, cohorted rollout strategy ("safety-gradient") that applies batching and KV-prefetch recommendations per-customer cohort with automatic rollback gates. We want to reduce per-token cost by ~10-25% on target workloads while keeping latency SLOs (p95 <= 250ms for interactive tiers) and error rates within baseline +/- 0.1 percentage points. Scope: hosted API and Dedicated serving lanes for models in the 7B–70B family. This ticket contains experiment design, instrumentation checklist, dashboard requirements, statistical test plan, and rollback playbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment infra can split traffic into dynamic cohorts and apply independent batching/prefetch configs
2) Metrics pipeline emits cohort-scoped tokens_per_request, cost_per_token, latency_p50/p95, 5xx_rate, and hallucination proxy metric (rerank delta)
3) Automated gate triggers will rollback cohort config when any gate breach persists for 3 consecutive 5-min windows
4) Dashboard shows real-time cohort health and a weekly report with cost savings and quality regressions
5) Statistical confidence: detect >=5% cost improvement with 90% power for top-20% traffic cohorts
steps: 1. Instrumentation: add cohort_id tagging in ingress router and propagate to tracing/telemetry
2. Create config manifest schema for batch_size, max_batch_delay_ms, kv_prefetch=true|false, prefetch_window_tokens
3. Build canary controller with safety-gradient policy: 0% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% in 30-min increments conditional on gate checks
4. Implement gate checks (latency, errors, hallucination proxy) and alarm publishers to experiment service
5. Launch 2-week experiment across 10 randomized cohorts (stratified by qps and sequence length distribution)
6. Collect per-cohort metrics, run analysis every 30 minutes, and pause rollout on gate breach
7. Post-experiment analysis: compute uplift and CI, log artifacts to Confluence and PRs to runtime repo
8. If stable, propose a staged product rollout and rollout policy codified in runtime-1.22 release notes
metrics: cost_per_1M_tokens: computed from billing_rate * tokens served / 1e6
tokens_per_request: average tokens generated+input per request
latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms: request end-to-end measured at ingress egress boundary
error_rate_5xx: proportion of requests with 5xx from runtime or network timeouts
success_ratio: fraction of requests meeting success criteria (p95 < threshold AND error_rate < threshold)
analysis_plan: Primary analysis uses sequential testing with group sequential boundaries: run a Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) for cost reduction vs. null. For latency and quality metrics, use nonparametric bootstrap to compute 95% CI per cohort. Control for multiple cohorts with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR at 10%. Produce per-cohort CSV export and an aggregated 'winner' recommendation. Use uplift = (baseline_cost - test_cost)/baseline_cost as primary effect size. For small cohorts (n<2000 requests/day) fallback to Bayesian posterior estimates with weakly informative priors.
rollback_triggers: 5xx_rate increases > 0.2 percentage points compared to baseline for 15 minutes
hallucination_proxy increase >= 5% with p<0.05 in bootstrap test
safety_gates: soft_gate: short-circuit increase to next cohort only after 2 stable windows (30 min total)
hard_gate: abort and rollback immediately on any hard trigger (5xx spike > 1% absolute)
rate_limit_guard: throttle batch-size-induced QPS surge to protect kernel saturation
